title: Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 Florida Panhandle Optimized Remediation Contract (ORC) and Military Munitions Response Program (MMRP)
description: This requirement is for comprehensive, performance-based environmental remediation activities to achieve Performance Objectives (PO's) at 58 Installation Restoration Program (IRP) sites and 5 Military Munitions Response Program (MMRP) sites at Eglin AFB, Hurlburt Field and Tyndall AFB in Florida. The range of services includes investigation, design, construction of remedial systems, operation and maintenance of established remedies, remedy optimization at applicable sites, and achievement of site-specific objectives.

Hood SPE60326R0519 Amendment 0001 Clauses 10.13.2026 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Wide Area Workflow (WAWF). This is a follow-on solicitation notice to sources sought notice SPE603-25-R-5X24 and SPE603-25-R-0525. This solicitation notice is for Fuel Operations Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Ft. Hood, TX. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. Tasks identified in the PWS are performed by either the Contractor or Government as specified in Section C-2.0 Performance Requirements. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. The NAICS Code for this procurement is 493190 and will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business. The period of performance is a four-year base period from December 1, 2026, through November 30, 2030, with a five-year option from December 1, 2030 through November 30, 2035, and a six-month option extension provision, December 1, 2035 through May 31, 2036. The Government anticipates awarding one Firm-Fixed Price contract. This information is subject to modification and in no way binds the Government to award a contract.

title: PANEL, STRUCTURAL, AIRCRAFT / NSN 1560-01-646-5441 / B-52 AIRCRAFT
description: A 100% Small Business Set-Aside solicitation will be issued to establish an Indefinite Quantity Contract (IQC) for NSN 1560-01-646-5441, a PANEL, STRUCUTRAL, AIRCRAFT. The award will be for a 5-year base period. The Estimated Annual Quantity (EAQ) is 40 EACH. Production units will be FOB: Destination; Inspection /Acceptance: Origin. Item is critical but not deemed a Critical Safety Item. Export Control applies. Surge does not apply. The proposed contract action is for supplies for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one or a limited number of sources under the authority of FAR 6.302. The OEM is Boeing (CAGE 81205) p/n 8-7849-11. Approved sources are H&R Parts Co. (CAGE 32821), Aero Components (CAGE 59213), Infinity Fabrication (CAGE 06DM5), Malones CNC Machining (CAGE 2V045) and DJ Engineering (CAGE 0C7H8). DLA Aviation does NOT possess complete technical data on this part. Any other interested manufacturing contractor would have to submit a Source Approval Request (SAR) package for approval to be added as a source by the assigned ESA. Interested persons may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all proposals received within forty-five days after date of publication of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Based upon market research, the Government is not using the policies contained in Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items, in its solicitation for the described supplies. However, interested persons may identify to the contracting officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial item within 15 days of this notice. This solicitation may include Procurement Note L09, Reverse Auction. Since a reverse auction may be conducted, offerors are encouraged to access the Procurex system and review the reverse auction help tutorials at https//dla.procurexinc.com to learn more about how to participate in an auction. In order to receive an award, regardless of dollar value, contractors must be registered in the System For Award Management (sam.gov). The final contract award decision may be based upon a combination of price, past performance and other evaluation factors as described in the solicitation. The estimated solicitation issue date is 11/16/2026. A copy of the solicitation will be available via DIBBS at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ on the issue date cited in the RFP. Choose the RFP you wish to download. RFPs are in portable document format (PDF). To download and view these documents you will need the latest version of Adobe Acrobat Reader. This software is available free at http://www.adobe.com. A paper copy of this solicitation will not be available to requesters.

title: 6505--Nitroglycerin SL Tablets (VA-27-00011802)
description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The VA Enterprise Procurement Office intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) 36E79727R0043 for an unrestricted procurement for Nitroglycerin Sublingual (SL) Tablets, for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) (inclusive of Consolidated Mail Order Pharmacies (CMOPs) and Option 2 State Veterans Homes (SVH)), Department of Defense (DoD) (inclusive of Tricare Mail Order Pharmacies (TMOPs)), Bureau of Prisons (BOP), Indian Health Service (IHS), and Federal Health Care Center (FHCC). VA will award one contract to the responsible offeror who will be able to provide an uninterrupted source of supply for the contracted items. The contract period will be for one year plus four pre-priced one-year option periods. The contract items will be distributed through the VA s and DOD s respective Pharmaceutical Prime Vendor Programs. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. Offerors must state the exact name (name that appears on label) by which the drug will be supplied and have an NDC number that is unique to the offeror. The successful offeror/contractor's label with its unique NDC shall be the only label on the product. Contractors shall not affix their label over another label on the product. VA labels must be able to securely adhere on top of the successful offeror/contractor s label. Solicitation # 36E79727R0043 will be electronically issued in commercial item format in accordance with FAR Part 12 approximately November 27, 2026, with a tentative closing date of December 11, 2026. The NAICS code for this procurement is 325412. Any future amendments and other miscellaneous documents will be available electronically for download at sam.gov. No paper copies of the solicitation will be available, and no telephone requests for paper copies of the solicitation will be accepted. Interested offerors are advised to continuously check Contracting Opportunities at SAM.gov for any changes to this solicitation. All responsible sources may submit an offer that if timely received, will be considered. The point of contact for this procurement is Alaina Anthony. Questions can be e-mailed to alaina.anthony@va.gov. description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command - Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC) in identifying industrial sources and capabilities to fabricate, fill and process (via commercial sterilization) a Group Serving Pouch (GSP), which will be included in the U.S. military�s Group Ration Platform. Specific Specifications: Capability to fabricate (or procure) GSPs, fill with vegetable and brine mixture, and commercially sterilize. Volumetric size of the GSP shall be between 24 to 144 ounces. Targeted shelf life of the pouch is 3 years at 80F Residual gas volume in the filled and sealed GSP shall not exceed 12% of the fill volume. The material used for the pouch shall be generally recognized as safe (GRAS) for use with food in accordance with 21 CFR, Parts 170-199 or other standards and regulations. The closure seal width shall be a minimum 1/8 inch for conventional heat seals or a minimum 1.0 mm for ultrasonic seals. The pouches shall be filled and hermetically sealed such that after thermal processing, the pouches shall withstand an internal pressure of 10 psig for 30 seconds, while the pouch is held between plates with a 2-inch distance between them. title: Trinkwasserkraftwerk Feschel
description:
Die Gemeinde Guttet-Feschel beabsichtigt, das Energiepotenzial des Quellwassers der Bachalpe hydroelektrisch zu nutzen. Mit dieser Idee wurde im Jahr 2023 die alte Trinkwasserleitung zwischen der Brunnen­stube auf der Bachalp auf ca. 2'000 m ü. M. und dem Druckbrecherschacht auf ca. 1'467 m ü. M. vollständig erneuert und als Druckleitung konzipiert. Das Projekt sieht vor, eine neue Zentrale an den bestehenden Druckbrecherschacht anzubauen. Von dort aus soll das turbinierte Quell­wasser direkt in den bestehenden Druckbrecherschacht drucklos eingeleitet werden.


Die vorliegende Ausschreibung beinhaltet die Planung (Engineering, Bemessung), Fertigung, Transport, Montage, Prüfung und Inbetriebnahme inkl. Schulung für die gesamten elektro­mechanischen Ausrüstungen für den Betrieb mit Trinkwasser beginnend vom bergseitigen Flansch vor dem Absperrorgan bis und mit Anschluss an den Klemmen der bauseits gelieferten NS-Verteilung in der Zentrale.


Weitere Informationen sind dem Beschrieb im Pflichtenheft zu entnehmen.

title: Polymerer til Frederikshavn Forsyning A/S
description: Frederikshavn Forsyning A/S inviterer ansøgere til at byde på nærværende 4-årige rammeaftale på levering af polymerer til afvanding af spildevandsslam på Ordregivers renseanlæg. En forudsætning for at kunne afgive tilbud - og dermed deltage i udbuddets tilbuds- og forhandlingsfase er, at virksomheden har ansøgt om at blive prækvalificeret, og at Ordregiver har vurderet, at virksomheden er egnet. Ordregiver vil herefter opfordre tilbudsgivere til at afgive tilbud i tilbudsfasen. Der er direkte adgang til udbudsmaterialet på udbudsportalen Comdia. Her vil spørgsmål/svar og tilrettede dokumenter ligeledes være tilgængelige. Ansøger er selv ansvarlig for, at ansøgningen lever op til alle krav og betingelser i udbudsmaterialet, og Ansøger bør være opmærksom på, at eventuelle uklarheder i oplysninger i Ansøgers tilbud kan tillægges negativ vægt ved vurdering af Ansøgers egnethed eller evaluering af tilbuddet. Rammeaftalen består i transport (levering) af polymerer til forafvanding og slutafvanding af spildevandsslam på de herunder beskrevne renseanlæg: Delaftale 1: •Skagen Renseanlæg (forafvanding) •Skagen Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) •Ålbæk Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) Delaftale 2: •Frederikshavn Renseanlæg (forafvanding) •Frederikshavn Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) •Sæby Renseanlæg (forafvanding) Delaftale 3: •Forrens GEM (flotation) Ordregiver ønsker at opnå et højt tørstof i det slutafvandede slam i kombination med tilfredsstillende rejektvandskvalitet og et lavt specifikt polymerforbrug. For yderligere specifikationer for de enkelte renseanlæg henvises der til Bilag 1 Kravspecifikation og Bilag 1A Fotografisk beskrivelse af slamafvandingsanlæg. Rammeaftalens forventede indkøbt polymermængde antages at blive: Delaftale 1: 193.200 kg Delaftale 2: 155.200 kg Delaftale 3: 58.000 kg Rammeaftalens maksimale indkøbt polymermængde udgør: Delaftale 1: 240.000 kg. Delaftale 2: 170.000 kg. Delaftale 3: 90.000 kg. Det er væsentligt at bemærke, at forbruget af polymer på Delaftale 1 og 3 i praksis afhænger meget af den modtagne mængde spildevand fra fiskeindustrien, hvorfor polymerforbruget her kan variere meget fra år til år. Dette er søgt indregnet i de stipulerede maksimale polymermængder. Det forventede årlige estimat udgør alene estimater, som ikke er bindende for Ordregiver. Dette betyder, at Ordregiver ikke forpligter sig ud over sit faktiske forbrug, som løbende kan ændre sig som følge af ændring af slammets egenskaber og løbende tildelinger baseret på afholdte tests jf. rammeaftalens proces for tildelinger af rekvisitioner. Ansøger vil således ikke være berettiget til positiv opfyldelsesinteresse eller på anden måde godtgørelse, hvis Ordregivers forbrug skulle ligge under det anførte estimat eller under Ansøgers forventninger. Ordregiver forventer at prækvalificere 5 ansøgere til deltagelse i tilbudsfasen. På baggrund af evalueringen af de indkomne tilbud i tilbudsfasen, forventer Ordregiver at indgå rammeaftale med to tilbudsgivere for hver delaftale. Såfremt der er flere ansøgere, der ikke er omfattet af én eller flere af udelukkelsesgrundene, og som opfylder minimumskravene til egnethedskriterierne, end ovenstående antal af tilbudsgivere, vil udvælgelsen af de ansøgere, der gives mulighed for at afgive tilbud, ske ud fra følgende kriterier: A.CV på tilbudte kontaktperson (kundeansvarlig) (50% vægtning) -Erfaring -Uddannelse B.Referencer jf. afsnit 11.2 i prækvalifikationsbetingelserne (50 % vægtning) -Sammenlignelige referencer med fokus på levering af polymerer til renseanlæg af tilsvarende størrelse Ansøger skal vedlægge særskilt CV for den tilbudte kontaktperson. CV må maksimalt fylde 1 A4-side (2400 tegn). Blandt de ansøgere, der opfylder minimumskravene til egnethed, foretager Ordregiver en vurdering af modtagne CV og referencerne under hvert vurderingstema. Vurderingen angår alene CV og referencernes relevans og styrke i forhold til den udbudte opgave og anvendes til at rangordne de egnede ansøgere. Under hvert vurderingstema tildeler Ordregiver en karakter fra 0 til 5. Karakteren for hvert vurderingstema multipliceres med temaets vægtning. De vægtede karakterer sammenlægges til en samlet score på maksimalt 6,00 point. Ansøgerne rangeres herefter efter deres samlede score. De ansøgere, der opnår de højeste samlede scorer, udvælges til at afgive tilbud. Såfremt to eller flere ansøgere opnår samme samlede score, rangeres ansøgerne efter deres score under vurderingstema A. Udvælgelsen foretages på grundlag af de oplysninger, som fremgår af Ansøgernes referencer. Det er Ansøgerens ansvar at beskrive referencerne tilstrækkeligt detaljeret til, at Ordregiver kan vurdere referencernes relevans og omfang i forhold til de enkelte vurderingstemaer. Yderligere beskrivelse af evalueringsmodel for udvælgelse af ansøgere fremgår af prækvalifikationsbetingelserne afsnit 12.

title: Germany – Engineering design services for mechanical and electrical installations for buildings – Fachplanungsleistungen für Technische Ausrüstung nach Teil 4 Abschnitt 2 HOAI, Anlagengruppen 4 und 5
description: Pfaffenwaldring 57, 70569 Stuttgart, Universität Stuttgart; NWZ II, Sanierung für Chemie, Fachplanungsleistungen für Technische Ausrüstung nach Teil 4 Abschnitt 2 HOAI, Anlagengruppen 4 und 5, Das Naturwissenschaftliche Zentrum (NWZ) I und II im Pfaffenwaldring (PWR) 55 und 57 in Stuttgart wurde in den 1970er Jahren fertiggestellt. Das NWZ soll in den kommenden Jahren abschnittsweise saniert werden. Gegenstand der ausgeschriebenen Planungsleistungen sind die elektrotechnischen Vorabmaßnahmen im NWZ I, die im Vorgriff auf die geplante Sanierung des NWZ II im ersten Sanierungsabschnitt erforderlich werden. Die Maßnahmen sind Bestandteil der Gesamtsanierungsmaßnahme NWZ. Im Zuge der Sanierung des NWZ II müssen bestehende Versorgungs- und technische Anlagen zwischen NWZ I und NWZ II getrennt, angepasst oder neu hergestellt werden. Darüber hinaus müssen bisher im NWZ II untergebrachte Nutzungen während der Sanierung interimsweise in das NWZ I verlagert werden. Hierfür sind die vorhandenen technischen Anlagen in den betreffenden Bereichen zu ertüchtigen bzw. vollständig neu aufzubauen. Gleichzeitig werden bestehende Nutzungen, insbesondere die Bibliothek, innerhalb des NWZ I verdichtet und neu organisiert. Im Laborhochhaus mit den angrenzenden Flachbauten des NWZ I ist im Wesentlichen die Fakultät Chemie untergebracht. In den Flachbauten befinden sich unter anderem Hörsäle, die Universitätsbibliothek und eine Cafeteria. Das NWZ I verfügt über insgesamt ca. 23.800 m² NUF (1-6). Die zur Bearbeitung vorgesehenen Bereiche umfassen insgesamt ca. 2.900 m² NUF und betreffen im Wesentlichen: die Neuordnung und Verdichtung der Universitätsbibliothek mit ca. 2.520 m² NUF, Verwaltungs- und Fachschaftsflächen mit ca. 90 m² NUF sowie Praktikums- und Laborflächen mit ca. 290 m² NUF. Aufgrund der erforderlichen Neuorganisation der Flucht- und Rettungswege sind zudem elektrotechnische Anlagen für temporäre Flucht- und Rettungswege zu planen. Hierzu gehören insbesondere die Beleuchtung und erforderliche Sicherheitsbeleuchtung der vorgesehenen Interims- Treppenhäuser einschließlich der Fluchtwege bis zu den Sammelplätzen. Die elektrotechnische Planung hat außerdem die Anpassung der Brandmeldeanlage an die veränderte Gebäudestruktur und die vorgesehenen Bauabschnitte zu berücksichtigen. Dies betrifft insbesondere die Abtrennung der Gebäudeteile, den Rückbau bzw. die Anpassung bestehender Melder und Leitungswege sowie erforderliche Interimslösungen während der Bauphase. Im Bereich der Bibliothek sind insbesondere die Beleuchtungsanlage, Stromversorgung, LAN-Verkabelung und WLAN-Infrastruktur an die zukünftige Nutzung und die geplante Nachverdichtung anzupassen. Für die in das NWZ I zu verlagernden Praktikums- und Laborflächen sind die elektrotechnischen Anlagen entsprechend den zukünftigen Nutzeranforderungen neu zu planen. Dies umfasst insbesondere die 230/ 400-V-Stromversorgung, Unterverteilungen, Endstromkreise, Beleuchtung, LAN-Verkabelung sowie die erforderlichen Anschlüsse für die technische Laborausstattung. Das Gebäude befindet sich größtenteils im Errichtungszustand und weist entsprechende bauzeitliche Schadstoffbelastungen auf. Die Umsetzung der Maßnahme erfolgt bei laufendem Universitäts- und Gebäudebetrieb. Die Aufrechterhaltung der Versorgung und des Betriebs der nicht von den jeweiligen Bauabschnitten betroffenen Bereiche ist während der gesamten Maßnahme sicherzustellen. Die Baukosten der Kostengruppen 440-450 betragen nach derzeitiger Kostenschätzung ca. 1.100.000 Euro. Der Projektstart ist mit der Auftragserteilung Anfang März 2027 vorgesehen. Die Fertigstellung der Maßnahme ist für das 1. Quartal 2031 vorgesehen. Beabsichtigt ist die Beauftragung von Fachplanungsleistungen nach Teil 4, Abschnitt 2 HOAI für die folgende zur Technischen Ausrüstung gehören Anlagengruppe nach § 53 Absatz 2 HOAI: Nr. 4 Starkstromanlagen und Nr. 5 Fernmelde- und informationstechnische Anlagen, Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 2 , 3 und 5 bis 8 sowie Besondere Leistungen.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Realisierungswettbewerb „Neubau Feuer- und Rettungswache“ in Lippstadt
description: Der derzeitige Standort der Feuer- und Rettungswache Lippstadt weist im Brandschutzbedarfsplan zahlreiche Mängel auf, u. a. das Fehlen von ausreichenden Flächen in verschiedenen Funktionsbereichen, die Unterbringungssituation für das Personal sowie die ungünstige Alarmausfahrten für Großfahrzeuge und stellt somit keine Zukunftsperspektive dar. Der politisch beschlossene neue Standort auf dem Uniongelände im Lippstädter Stadtgebiet bietet hinsichtlich der Erreichbarkeit für die ehrenamtlichen Einsatzkräfte und die größtmögliche Flächenabdeckung und kürzeste Eintreffzeit aus Sicht des Hauptamtes geeignete Voraussetzungen. Der zu errichtende Neubau der weiterhin kombinierten Feuer- und Rettungswache Lippstadt mit hauptamtlichen Kräften soll auf dem südlichen Bereich des Uniongeländes zukunftsfähig die notwendigen Arbeitsbedingungen für das hauptberufliche Einsatzpersonal Brandschutz und Rettungsdienst sowie die ehrenamtlichen Einsatzkräfte sicherstellen, um bei Notlagen jeglicher Art die entsprechende Hilfeleistung zu gewährleisten. Das gesamte Raumprogramm umfasst ein Flächensoll von ca. 7.850 m² zzgl. entwurfsabhängiger Flächen, das in Summe 46 Stellplätze in den Fahrzeughallen und die Waschhalle beinhaltet. Ziel des Wettbewerbes ist es, über alternative und optimierte Konzepte, die den unterschiedlichen Anforderungen in gleicher Weise gerecht werden, ein/e geeignete/n AuftragnehmerIn (ArchitektIn) für die weiteren Planungsleistungen zu finden.

title: Denmark – Chemical products – Polymerer til Frederikshavn Forsyning A/S
description: Frederikshavn Forsyning A/S inviterer ansøgere til at byde på nærværende 4-årige rammeaftale på levering af polymerer til afvanding af spildevandsslam på Ordregivers renseanlæg. En forudsætning for at kunne afgive tilbud - og dermed deltage i udbuddets tilbuds- og forhandlingsfase er, at virksomheden har ansøgt om at blive prækvalificeret, og at Ordregiver har vurderet, at virksomheden er egnet. Ordregiver vil herefter opfordre tilbudsgivere til at afgive tilbud i tilbudsfasen. Der er direkte adgang til udbudsmaterialet på udbudsportalen Comdia. Her vil spørgsmål/svar og tilrettede dokumenter ligeledes være tilgængelige. Ansøger er selv ansvarlig for, at ansøgningen lever op til alle krav og betingelser i udbudsmaterialet, og Ansøger bør være opmærksom på, at eventuelle uklarheder i oplysninger i Ansøgers tilbud kan tillægges negativ vægt ved vurdering af Ansøgers egnethed eller evaluering af tilbuddet. Rammeaftalen består i transport (levering) af polymerer til forafvanding og slutafvanding af spildevandsslam på de herunder beskrevne renseanlæg: Delaftale 1: •Skagen Renseanlæg (forafvanding) •Skagen Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) •Ålbæk Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) Delaftale 2: •Frederikshavn Renseanlæg (forafvanding) •Frederikshavn Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) •Sæby Renseanlæg (forafvanding) Delaftale 3: •Forrens GEM (flotation) Ordregiver ønsker at opnå et højt tørstof i det slutafvandede slam i kombination med tilfredsstillende rejektvandskvalitet og et lavt specifikt polymerforbrug. For yderligere specifikationer for de enkelte renseanlæg henvises der til Bilag 1 Kravspecifikation og Bilag 1A Fotografisk beskrivelse af slamafvandingsanlæg. Rammeaftalens forventede indkøbt polymermængde antages at blive: Delaftale 1: 193.200 kg Delaftale 2: 155.200 kg Delaftale 3: 58.000 kg Rammeaftalens maksimale indkøbt polymermængde udgør: Delaftale 1: 240.000 kg. Delaftale 2: 170.000 kg. Delaftale 3: 90.000 kg. Det er væsentligt at bemærke, at forbruget af polymer på Delaftale 1 og 3 i praksis afhænger meget af den modtagne mængde spildevand fra fiskeindustrien, hvorfor polymerforbruget her kan variere meget fra år til år. Dette er søgt indregnet i de stipulerede maksimale polymermængder. Det forventede årlige estimat udgør alene estimater, som ikke er bindende for Ordregiver. Dette betyder, at Ordregiver ikke forpligter sig ud over sit faktiske forbrug, som løbende kan ændre sig som følge af ændring af slammets egenskaber og løbende tildelinger baseret på afholdte tests jf. rammeaftalens proces for tildelinger af rekvisitioner. Ansøger vil således ikke være berettiget til positiv opfyldelsesinteresse eller på anden måde godtgørelse, hvis Ordregivers forbrug skulle ligge under det anførte estimat eller under Ansøgers forventninger. Ordregiver forventer at prækvalificere 5 ansøgere til deltagelse i tilbudsfasen. På baggrund af evalueringen af de indkomne tilbud i tilbudsfasen, forventer Ordregiver at indgå rammeaftale med to tilbudsgivere for hver delaftale. Såfremt der er flere ansøgere, der ikke er omfattet af én eller flere af udelukkelsesgrundene, og som opfylder minimumskravene til egnethedskriterierne, end ovenstående antal af tilbudsgivere, vil udvælgelsen af de ansøgere, der gives mulighed for at afgive tilbud, ske ud fra følgende kriterier: A.CV på tilbudte kontaktperson (kundeansvarlig) (50% vægtning) -Erfaring -Uddannelse B.Referencer jf. afsnit 11.2 i prækvalifikationsbetingelserne (50 % vægtning) -Sammenlignelige referencer med fokus på levering af polymerer til renseanlæg af tilsvarende størrelse Ansøger skal vedlægge særskilt CV for den tilbudte kontaktperson. CV må maksimalt fylde 1 A4-side (2400 tegn). Blandt de ansøgere, der opfylder minimumskravene til egnethed, foretager Ordregiver en vurdering af modtagne CV og referencerne under hvert vurderingstema. Vurderingen angår alene CV og referencernes relevans og styrke i forhold til den udbudte opgave og anvendes til at rangordne de egnede ansøgere. Under hvert vurderingstema tildeler Ordregiver en karakter fra 0 til 5. Karakteren for hvert vurderingstema multipliceres med temaets vægtning. De vægtede karakterer sammenlægges til en samlet score på maksimalt 6,00 point. Ansøgerne rangeres herefter efter deres samlede score. De ansøgere, der opnår de højeste samlede scorer, udvælges til at afgive tilbud. Såfremt to eller flere ansøgere opnår samme samlede score, rangeres ansøgerne efter deres score under vurderingstema A. Udvælgelsen foretages på grundlag af de oplysninger, som fremgår af Ansøgernes referencer. Det er Ansøgerens ansvar at beskrive referencerne tilstrækkeligt detaljeret til, at Ordregiver kan vurdere referencernes relevans og omfang i forhold til de enkelte vurderingstemaer. Yderligere beskrivelse af evalueringsmodel for udvælgelse af ansøgere fremgår af prækvalifikationsbetingelserne afsnit 12.

title: Keyport Infrastructure Security Support Services Solicitation
description: *This Solicitation is for SEAPORT NXG MAC HOLDERS ONLY. No other offers will be considered. Seaport MAC Holders will need to register for PIEE accounts in order to submit offers.*Naval Undersea Warfare Center (NUWC) Division Keyport is soliciting a task order for Keyport Infrastructure Security Support Services (KISSS). This requirement supports the Infrastructure Services Division (Code 102) and the Security Division (Code 105).The scope of work includes, but is not limited to: Safety Compliance, Environmental Compliance, Facilities Engineering, Facilities Planning, Facilities Management, Facilities Maintenance, Security Operations Support, and Monitoring Support. The selected contractor will support Code 102 in its mission to plan, manage, and maintain NUWC Division Keyports safety, environmental, and facilities programs, while also providing security services under the direction of the Code 105 Security Office. The contemplated task order will be a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) under the SeaPort NxG allowing any small business company in SeaPort to propose. It will be awarded on a best value basis to the Government. A trade-off analysis will be carried out, taking into consideration technical capability, past performance, and cost/price. It will include a base period of twelve (12) months and may include up to four (4) option years. The solicitation is set aside for Seaport Small businesses. The applicable PSC code for this requirement is R499 and the applicable NAICS code is 541330. The task order is predicted to be awarded in November 2027 with a predicted start date of January 2028. The support services are currently being performed under SeaPort-NxG task order N0025322F3001 by McLaughlin Research Corporation.

title: USACE Moorings Life Safety Improvement Project
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT and is for informational/market research purposes only. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, QUOTATION OR BID, NOR A SYNOPSIS OF A PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION UNDER FAR SUBPART 5.2. This Sources Sought is to gain knowledge of the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of industry so the Government can make informed business decisions. We are seeking responses from both large and small business members of industry to include: Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses to include 8(a) firms, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone), Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB) to include Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small business (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB). All interested parties are highly encouraged to respond. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) for this requirement is: TBD. The approximate value of Project will be $5 to $25M. Formal Sources Sought Response Due � before 3:00 pm Pacific on December 18th 2026. 1. Project Details and Background The project is to upgrade the administration buildings at the US Government Moorings located on the west bank of the Willamette River (River Miles 6.08 to 6.21). This facility serves as the primary port, repair and supply base for the USACE Portland District Fleet, including dredges and hydro survey vessels. After a major fire at the facility, the Government is pursuing life safety and seismic upgrades to the facility. 2. Project Scope This project will involve upgrading the Fire Protection systems to the Administration building, Machine Shop, Warehouse, Weld Shop, and sprinkler system to the Administration building and Weld shop and adding site lighting. This would also include life safety and code improvements within the same buildings. Anticipated Construction Schedule: CENWP intends to advertise in May 2027 and award in July 2027. Construction Contract with estimated construction completion by the end of calendar year 2028. Estimated Construction Cost (ECC): The current ECC is between $5,000,000 to $25,000,000 Number and Type of Contracts: NWP contemplates awarding one (1), Firm Fixed-Price contract. The acquisition strategy decision has not yet been determined. Maximum small business participation is being sought at both the Prime and subcontracting levels. Anticipated Source Selection Process: The expected method to determine the best value to the government is Invitation for Bid. Project Details: The following information represents the project objectives: Improve the life safety of the facilities at the US. Government Moorings. 3. Submission Instructions. Formal responses to this Sources Sought notice must be submitted electronically by e-mail to SUBJECT: US Moorings Life Safety Upgrade to Ian Lutjens at Ian.k.Lutjens@usarmy.mil and Brandon Lasich at Brandon.M.Lasich@usace.army.mil Interested parties� responses to this Sources Sought shall be limited to six (6) pages and shall include the following information: Experience in installing fire control systems. Experience in installing Sprinkler systems. Retro fitting new health life safety systems into an older building. Upgrading utilities in an older building 4. Disclaimer and Important Notes. This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow up information. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's capabilities to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or to provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. All interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://www.sam.gov to have size status considered. You must remain current for the duration of the source selection process to be eligible for award of a Government contract.

title: Request for Information (RFI) - Commercial Loan Servicing and Asset Administration Services
description: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), Division of Resolutions and Receiverships (DRR), is conducting market research to identify qualified firms capable of providing commercial loan and asset servicing, administration, and resolution support services for large-volume domestic portfolios. Services may involve portfolios exceeding 10,000 assets and approximately $25 billion in aggregate book value. The FDIC is particularly interested in industry's ability to rapidly assume servicing responsibility for complex commercial loan portfolios, including portfolios associated with failed financial institutions, bridge banks, receiverships, and other resolution-related environments. Portfolios may include Commercial Real Estate (CRE), Commercial and Industrial (C&I), Acquisition, Development, and Construction (ADC), agricultural, government-guaranteed, syndicated and participation loans, specialty banking assets, servicing rights, securitized assets, ORE/REO assets, and performing, delinquent, non-performing, or matured loans. Services may include portfolio onboarding and transfer, loan administration, payment processing, collections, workout and restructuring activities, collateral management, foreclosure and liquidation support, asset disposition support, reporting, and related servicing functions. Interested parties are requested to complete and submit (Appendix A) �RFI LBS � Commercial� as their primary response. Respondents may also provide supplemental capability information. The FDIC strongly encourages use of the Appendix A template to facilitate efficient and consistent market research analysis. The FDIC is particularly interested in information regarding: Servicing capacity and scalability Portfolio transfer and onboarding experience Government-guaranteed loan servicing experience Receivership, resolution, workout, and asset disposition experience Cybersecurity capabilities Recommended contract structures and performance metrics Industry best practices and risk considerations Responses are encouraged from commercial loan servicers, financial institutions, specialty servicers, asset managers, and other organizations with relevant experience and capabilities. DISCLAIMER: This Sources Sought Notice is issued for market research and information-gathering purposes. This notice does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or a commitment by the FDIC to award a contract. Responses will be used solely to support acquisition planning and assess industry capabilities. The FDIC will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response to this notice.

title: Strategic Technology Office-wide Innovation Solutions Opening Announcement
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) anticipates funding a limited number of proposals under this solicitation. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. Proposed research should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. The Strategic Technology Office (STO) at DARPA regularly publishes solicitations requesting responses to specific program topics. This announcement seeks revolutionary research ideas for topics not addressed by ongoing STO programs or other published DARPA solicitations. To avoid proposals that duplicate existing activities or are responsive to other published STO solicitations, potential proposers are highly encouraged to review current STO programs and solicitations, respectively listed at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/offices/sto and http://www.darpa.mil/work-with-us/opportunities. Contacting STO program managers to discuss their research interests is also encouraged. A current list of program managers is available at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/people. This Innovation Solutions Opening solicits under the procurement authorities of 10 U.S. Code � 4001, 10 U.S.C. � 4021, 10 U.S.C. � 4022, and 10 U.S.C. � 4023, that allow procurement activities authority to enter into agreements with industry, academia, and other organizations to fund research and development through cooperative agreements, Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research, OTAs for prototypes, and procurement for experimental purposes. Proposals received as a result of this Innovation Solutions Opening will be evaluated by the Government in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified herein through a scientific review process. DARPA solicitations are posted on the SAM website under the Contract Opportunities link at https://sam.gov/. The following information is for those wishing to respond to the Innovation Solutions Opening. 1.1. STO MISSION AND THRUST AREAS DARPA's STO is a systems warfare office that seeks innovative and disruptive technologies for existing and future battlespaces. STO programs deliver solutions at speed and scale for today's warfighters while developing the resilient "breakthrough" systems and technologies across all physical domains (Air, Space, Sea, and Land) and across the spectrum of competition. STO does not focus on one area of responsibility or phenomenology. Instead, STO programs capture the strategic, logistical, and tactical complexity of today's national security environments. STO seeks to create new "proof-of-concept" mission systems. 1.2. TOPIC AREAS OF INTEREST Research areas of current interest to STO include, but are not limited to, the following topics: � Acoustic communication and sensing � Adaptability � Advanced computing � Additive manufacturing � Architecture and advanced systems engineering � Artificial intelligence � Autonomy and control algorithms � Combat identification � Command and control (C2) � Communications and networking, virtual and adaptive � Complexity management � Critical infrastructure defense � Decision aids and C2 technology � DevOps and novel software development and integration � Directed energy (DE) � Distributed autonomy and teaming (machine-machine, human-machine) � Economic security � Effects chain functions (disaggregated find, fix, track, target, engage, assess) � Electro-optic/infrared sensors � Electromagnetic warfare (EW) � High-frequency (HF) communications and sensing � High voltage electric power systems and architecture � Human behavior modeling � Human-machine symbiosis � Industrial engineering � Integration and reliability technologies � Interoperability � Logistics � Modeling and simulation � Microwave and millimeter wave communications and sensing � Novel kinetic effects � Non-kinetic effects (EW, DE, cyber) � Optical technologies � Photonics � Radio technologies (especially software-defined and novel waveforms and processing) � Radar and adaptive arrays � Resilient systems � Robotics � Seekers and other expendable sensors and processing � Sensors and analytics � Signal processing � Space sensors, communications, autonomy, and architectures (especially supporting proliferated low earth orbit constellations) � Strategy analysis technology � Supply chain analytics � System of systems � Undersea and seabed technology � Tactics development technology � Testing and data collection � Very low earth orbit (VLEO) technology � Very low frequency (VLF) technology

title: Enterprise Wide IT Support Services
description: The Department of the Navy, NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Norfolk, Philadelphia Office, on behalf of the Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI), intends to solicit and award a task order for full-spectrum lifecycle Enterprise-Wide Information Technology (EWIT) Support Services. This posting serves as the formal public notification of the Government's Notice of Intent to Consolidate and Substantially Bundle Requirements in accordance with FAR 7.107-5 and DFARS 205.205-70. The prospective acquisition consolidates ten (10) active legacy task orders into a single, comprehensive task order. 2. Scope of Services To operate, maintain, secure, modernize, integrate, and enhance enterprise IT capabilities supporting mission operations, the Contractor will perform work across the following defined service domains: Enterprise Architecture, Assessment, Verification, and Transition: Architecture, technical assessment, independent verification, configuration-baseline, operational-readiness, transition, and technical analysis activities. IT Systems Engineering, Operations, and Sustainment: Engineering, operations, sustainment, modernization, migration, integration, and optimization support for designated IT systems and services. This includes cloud and hybrid-environment engineering, tenant/workload onboarding, infrastructure, backup/recovery, DevSecOps implementation, and identity/access security tool integration. Application Development and Sustainment: Development, modernization, sustainment, integration, migration, deployment, enhancement, and decommissioning of designated mission and business applications using commercial, Government, open-source, cloud-native, and traditional computing technologies. Data Services: Data-management, data-platform, data-engineering, data-science, analytics, automation, super-intelligence/machine-learning, visualization, and secure data-transport support. Cybersecurity Services: Cybersecurity engineering, compliance, authorization-support, assessment, remediation, monitoring, and incident-support services (including Risk Management Framework (RMF) lifecycle support and authorization artifact development). Program, Service Management, and Transition: Program and service-management support directly associated with performance, including contract-management planning, schedule/risk/dependency tracking, configuration/change control, and transition-in/transition-out support. 3. Operational & Security Environments As defined in the Sources Sought documentation, performance of these services is subject to the following operating conditions: Network & Infrastructure Environments: Performance may occur across Government-designated classified and unclassified networks; cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments; enterprise applications; data platforms; communications environments; and geographically dispersed operating locations. Cloud Architecture: The operational environment utilizes industry-standard cloud service provider infrastructure, platform, and serverless capabilities at various impact and classification levels. Personnel Security Requirements: The anticipated effort requires a fully cleared workforce meeting Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) eligibility and access requirements at contract start for positions requiring such access. 4. Acquisition Strategy & Schedule Period of Performance: One-year base period with four (4) one-year option periods (total of 5 years). Target Solicitation / Award Timeline: Estimated award date is May 1, 2027.

description: Anhydrous Calcium Sulfate (USG Snow White) 1. Introduction and Background 1.1 Purpose The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Armaments Center (DEVCOM AC), located at Picatinny Arsenal, NJ, is issuing this Sources Sought Notice as a market research tool under the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) framework of FAR Part 10. The primary objective of this announcement is to identify potential sources possessing the capability, technical expertise, and capacity to manufacture, package, and deliver Anhydrous Calcium Sulfate in support of mission-critical ballistic evaluation activities.This market survey is being conducted for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a Request for Proposal (RFP), an Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. 1.2 Operational Background DEVCOM AC serves as the primary research, development, and engineering center for advanced armament systems, munitions, and related technologies. To support testing, quality assurance, and ongoing evaluation operations at the Ballistic Evaluation Center (BEC) at Picatinny Arsenal, the Government has an ongoing operational requirement for high-purity Anhydrous Calcium Sulfate. title: TECHNOLOGY/BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY: A MOPA Fiber Laser Platform for Solid-State Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography Driver Lasers
description: Opportunity: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), operated by the Lawrence Livermore National Security (LLNS), LLC under contract no. DE-AC52-07NA27344 (Contract 44) with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), is offering the opportunity to enter into a collaboration to further develop and commercialize its A MOPA Fiber Laser Platform for Solid-State Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography Driver Lasers. Background: Among the lowest-hanging fruits for improving the wall-plug efficiency (and therefore economic viability) and increasing the throughput of the EUV process is improving either the wall-plug efficiency of the EUV laser source itself or improving the laser-to-EUV conversion efficiency using optimized pulse shapes. The current state-of-the-art uses discharge-driven carbon dioxide lasers operating at 10.6 micron to hit the target (tin droplet) with one or more pre-pulses to flatten the droplet in the direction of laser propagation, followed by a high-energy (~ 1 J) main pulse to produce EUV. Description: This MOPA invention is primarily to seed a Tm:YLF laser chain that will amplify the laser pulses up to the ~ 1 J level for EUV generation. The arbitrary pulse shaping capability will be used to optimize EUV generation efficiency. The proposed laser front end will also be capable of precompensating for square pulse distortion in high-energy (> 100 J) Tm:YLF or Tm:YAG lasers. Additional applications spaces include seeding lasers (all-fiber or solid state) for medical devices (laser-assisted surgery), laser drilling, LIDAR, and standoff detection. Advantages/Benefits: The arbitrary pulse shaping capability allows tailoring of the laser pulse shape on timescales ranging from 100 ps to milliseconds, a capability that can be used to tune the pulse shape to increase the efficiency of EUV generation or radiation generation using other target materials besides tin. Potential Applications: EUV Sources lasers, additional applications spaces include seeding lasers (all-fiber or solid state) for medical devices (laser-assisted surgery), laser drilling, LIDAR, and standoff detection. description: Description of Services: This non-personal services requirement supports the U.S. Army Medical Command�s Neurocognitive Assessment Program by providing neurocognitive assessment and support services for Department of War (DoW) agencies, including the Army, Navy/Marine Corps, Air Force, and Space Force, with potential future support to the U.S. Coast Guard. description: Description of Services: This non-personal services requirement supports the U.S. Army Medical Command�s Neurocognitive Assessment Program by providing neurocognitive assessment and support services for Department of War (DoW) agencies, including the Army, Navy/Marine Corps, Air Force, and Space Force, with potential future support to the U.S. Coast Guard. The contractor will provide baseline and periodic reassessment testing for Service Members (SMs) throughout their careers, new accessions at Initial Military Training sites, and DoW civilian employees in at-risk occupations or locations, as well as assessments and reassessments for SMs with head injuries, potentially concussive exposures, symptoms indicating possible brain injury, or other hazards to brain health. Z2DA--FY27 Minor Diagnostics Imaging Center Expansion Vegas 593-407
description: INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting proposals and subsequently awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract for the design-bid-build minor construction project #593-407, Diagnostic Imaging Center Expansion Minor Construction at VA Southern Nevada Healthcare System (VASNHS) located at 6900 North Pecos Rd., North Las Vegas, NV 89086. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The contractor shall provide all tools, equipment, materials, labor, supervision, and management to complete the construction of a new 2-story expansion and renovation to expand the Radiology Department and integrate with the Emergency Department. Construction practices shall comply with all VA solicitation drawings and specifications, VA regulations, procedures, and conditions for work at the medical center and any applicable codes as per requirements of all governing agencies. This project shall construct a new 2- story 11,282 square foot Diagnostic Imaging Center Expansion and renovate 870 square feet of an adjacent storage room and exam space in the Emergency Department to expand the Radiology Department and integrate the two spaces. The first floor will consist of a state-of-the-Art facility fully equipped for provisions or services to house (2) MRI, CT, X-ray, Ultrasound, Administrations and Support spaces to support the Radiology Department. The second floor will be an extension of the existing penthouse that services the Emergency Department. The project will include the relocation of existing utilities that encroach into the building footprint of the new expansion as shown on the design documents. Work includes general construction, alterations, and certain other items. Services include but not limited to furnish all supervision, labor, equipment, materials, and transportation necessary to accomplish work for the demolition and replacement as required by specifications and drawings. Contractor shall complete the intent of project 593-407 in strict accordance with the SOW, drawings, and specifications. All work not specifically identified by the drawings and/or specifications but necessary for a complete system shall be included as if specifically identified in the Contract Documents. ADMINISTRATIVE The solicitation will be issued as a Request for Proposals (RFP) conducted in accordance with FAR part 15 and will be evaluated in accordance with the tradeoff procedures listed in the solicitation. The solicitation will be issued as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Offers received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45.0 million. The solicitation will be issued in late Nov 2026. The period of performance is approximately 480 calendar days from the issuance of the notice to proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000. This notice is not a request for competitive offers. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to Jessica.stevenson3@va.gov. Telephone calls will not be accepted.

title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Heat Pipe Reactor Fire Mitigation and Suppression System
description: The Heat Pipe Reactor Fire Mitigation and Suppression System from Los Alamos National Laboratory, transforms the heat pipes inside an alkali metal-cooled nuclear reactor from passive thermal conduits into active, sensor-driven fire defense components, giving designers of advanced small and microreactors a layered, automated safeguard against one of the most challenging hazards in their systems. By combining an inert gas buffer, a phase change material jacket, automated suppressant injection at multiple points and optional neutron-absorber dispersion into the reactor core, the system delivers redundant protection that responds within milliseconds of detecting fire-like conditions. This system enables advanced reactor developers to meet stringent safety expectations for remote, unattended and space-constrained deployments without redesigning the core architecture around bulky external suppression equipment. How it Works During normal operation, each heat pipe carries thermal energy away from the reactor core through the evaporation and condensation of an alkali metal working fluid, while valves connecting the heat pipe to external suppressant chambers remain closed. Temperature and pressure sensors continuously monitor the heat pipe reactor core and the valves near each heat pipe end, feeding data to a controller that compares readings against predefined thresholds. When a reading crosses the first threshold, the controller opens a valve and forces a fire suppressant material, typically a boron compound, into the interior of the heat pipe. If conditions worsen and a second threshold is crossed, additional valves activate to inject suppressant from the opposite end of the heat pipe, evacuate the working fluid through a dedicated valve and release suppressant into an inert gas chamber that annularly surrounds the heat pipe at the heat exchanger interface. Technical Description The system architecture centers on a heat pipe reactor core engaging a plurality of dual-ended or single-ended heat pipes, where both ends of each heat pipe extend externally of the core block so that suppressant can be introduced from either side of the core. A heat exchanger device sits at the heat rejection end of each heat pipe and defines an enclosed inert gas chamber that annularly surrounds the heat pipe, creating a physical gap between the alkali metal working fluid and any water-based cooling fluid. The chamber adds a second point of failure that must occur before incompatible fluids can interact, and the inert gas itself can serve as a blanketing agent for active flames. A layer of phase change material, typically a salt that doubles as a Class D fire extinguishing agent and alkali metal fire retardant, is disposed on the outer surface of the gas chamber, partitioned by fin-bearing components that both store thermal energy and improve heat transfer to the surrounding cooling fluid. The active suppression and shutdown logic is governed by a controller comprising memory, processor, input/output circuitry and communications circuitry, optionally implemented as a distributed or cloud-based system. First and second valves regulate suppressant flow into each end of the heat pipe interior cavity from dedicated suppressant chambers, while third and fourth valves regulate suppressant flow into the inert gas chamber from separate chambers. The second valve at the heat pipe�s far end can also be configured to evacuate working fluid either simultaneously with or prior to suppressant injection, encouraging dispersion of the suppressant throughout the pipe. As an additional shutdown pathway, the reactor core block can include gaps between fuel rods and heat pipes in which a neutron absorber material such as cadmium or a boron compound is preloaded; on detection of an alkali metal fire, the controller can release that absorber into the gaps to reduce core reactivity and aid shutdown, providing a coupled fire-and-reactivity response unique to this design. Advantages Multiple independent barriers between reactive alkali metals and potential ignition sources, reducing the probability of a single-point failure Automated, sensor-driven response that opens valves and injects suppressant within milliseconds of fire-like conditions being detected Dual-purpose phase change jacket that stores thermal energy during normal operation and acts as a fire retardant during an event Coupled fire suppression and reactor shutdown through optional neutron absorber dispersion into the core Flexible architecture compatible with both heat pipe-cooled reactor cores and auxiliary equipment such as molten salt pumps Configurable suppressant choices and threshold logic, allowing developers to tailor the response to their specific reactor design Market Applications Nuclear Energy (microreactors, small modular reactors, heat pipe-cooled designs) Power Generation (remote bases, mining sites, Arctic installations) Space and Lunar Surface Power (radioisotope and fission surface power systems) Industrial Process Heat (high-temperature manufacturing, hydrogen production facilities) Marine and Naval Propulsion (advanced compact reactor concepts for maritime use) Nuclear Safety Instrumentation (sensor and controller subsystems for licensed reactor operators) Development Status: TRL 3 U.S. Patent No. 12,640,276 LA-UR-26-25100 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL�s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov. title: TECHNOLOGY/BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY: Heavy Rare Earth Binding Proteins
description: Opportunity: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), operated by the Lawrence Livermore National Security (LLNS), LLC under contract no. DE-AC52-07NA27344 (Contract 44) with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), is offering the opportunity to enter into a collaboration to further develop and commercialize its Heavy Rare Earth Binding Proteins. Background: Rare earth elements (REEs) are critically required for high tech as well as defense applications. Therefore, building a resilient domestic supply chain for REEs is a national security imperative. Lanmodulin (LanM), a bacterial protein, and its variants provide a biotechnology approach for REE extraction as they have a very high specificity and affinity for REEs. Not all REEs are equally rare and equally critical. Criticality between the light REEs (LREs) and heavy REEs (HREs) varies by several orders of magnitude and depends on their relative abundance and market price. For instance, HREs are ~8,000 times more critical than LREs because HREs are 200x rarer and 40x more valuable than LREs. More than 98% of world's refined HREs come from China. The supply chain disruption of HREs Lu, Dy, Tb and Gd (4 of top 10 most at-risk materials) is predicted to have a total of $6.25 Billion net loss in GDP/year. Considering that naturally occurring LanMs have higher affinity for LREs, there is an unmet need for HRE-selective LanMs. Description: The inventors have discovered a new class of LanMs that enable HRE-selective bulk capture of the most valuable and rare REs found in feedstocks. Using a combination of machine learning approaches, the inventors designed 500 new lanmodulins out of which 54 showed HRE-selective binding. The best candidate has a separation factor (Lu/La) of 4.61, almost five-fold selectivity for HREs and has only 30% sequence identity with the prototype LanM, Mex LanM. Advantages/Benefits: Novel LanMs have significantly higher selectivity for HRE as compared to LREs Enable HRE-selective bulk capture of the most valuable and rare REEs found in feedstocks Potential Applications: Pre-concentration of HREs from ore leachates Processing dilute, high-volume REE feedstocks E-waste HRE recovery and closed loop recycling of magnet leachates Total high volume REE recovery from transitional-metal rich solutions Replacing solvent-based extraction processes Development Status: Current stage of technology development: TRL ? 0-2 ? 3-5 ? 5-9 LLNL has filed for patent protection on this invention. title: TECHNOLOGY/BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY: Ultraviolet or Thermally Curable Fluoropolymers Formulations with Controlled Macro-, Meso- and Micro-Porosity
description: Opportunity: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), operated by the Lawrence Livermore National Security (LLNS), LLC under contract no. DE-AC52-07NA27344 (Contract 44) with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), is offering the opportunity to enter into a collaboration to further develop and commercialize its thermally curable, porous fluoropolymer formulations for advanced manufacturing. Background: Fluoropolymers are commercially important materials known for their nonstick, low-friction surfaces. They also offer excellent chemical resistance, strong mechanical properties, high-temperature performance, and dielectric strength. The two primary commercial porous fluoropolymers are expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) and sintered polytetrafluoroethylene (sPTFE), which differ primarily in their microscale structures. Both ePTFE and sPTFE are difficult to process and require specialized equipment. As a result, they are generally limited to relatively simple geometries, such as cylindrical or planar forms. Fluoropolymers containing substantial air-filled voids form microporous structures that enable gas transport and can increase dielectric strength relative to bulk, nonporous materials. At the same time, the fluoropolymer matrix, particularly in commonly used ePTFE, retains its ability to repel liquids and water. Description: LLNL researchers have developed porous fluoropolymer formulations that can be patterned into arbitrary three-dimensional structures using casting, conformal coating, molding, and additive manufacturing. The formulations may be thermoplastic or thermosetting and can be cured using external stimuli, including thermal or photochemical processes. These formulations incorporate a sacrificial material, or porogen, that generates nanoscale to microscale porosity in the cured fluoropolymer. Porogens may be added before curing or formed during curing through intrinsic chemical reactions. They are removed during or after curing, leaving a nanoporous or microporous structure within the fluoropolymer matrix. Both unfilled and porogen-containing fluoropolymer feedstocks can be processed using 3D-printing techniques. For a given porogen, the morphology and geometry of the resulting pores can be controlled by adjusting the curing conditions and the porogen-to-fluoropolymer ratio. Advantages/Benefits: Multiscale porous structures: Enables the creation and control of three-dimensional porous fluoropolymers at multiple length scales using thermally or photochemically curable thermosetting resins. Tailored material properties: Provides greater control over component geometry, pore structure, and resulting material properties through formulation chemistry and manufacturing processes. Simplified, flexible manufacturing: Expands the design space while simplifying fabrication by enabling casting, coating, molding, and 3D printing of porous fluoropolymers. Potential Applications: Wearable fabrics/waterproofing. Biomedical applications, including patches, lipoatrophy implants, sutures, lead assemblies, stents and dental floss. Gas diffusion layers in many electrochemical energy storage. Development Status: Current stage of technology development: TRL3 LLNL has filed for patent protection on this invention. title: Iceland – Application service providers – Billing and Rating Solution for Rarik ohf.
description: Rarik ohf., an electricity distribution operator in Iceland, is procuring a cloud-hosted electricity billing and rating solution to replace its existing billing system. The solution will serve approximately 50,000 metering points and support the processing of approximately 50,000 invoices per month. The contract includes implementation, licensing, support and maintenance. The solution must support configurable tariffs and charges, automated billing runs, validation and exception handling, and an audit trail for billing data and corrections. It must integrate with Rarik’s meter data management, customer management, finance and reporting systems through documented, standards-based interfaces. The contract may also include an optional meter data management solution, as detailed in the invitation to tender. The procurement is conducted as a negotiated procedure with prior call for competition. Interested economic operators are invited to submit a request to participate. Shortlisted candidates will subsequently be invited to submit tenders.
